message.content:
On average, a healthy adult human brain weighs roughly **1.30 – 1.40 kilograms** (about **2.9 – 3.0 pounds**).  

Key points:

| Factor | Typical effect on weight |
|--------|--------------------------|
| Sex | Males tend to have slightly heavier brains (~1.36 kg) than females (~1.32 kg), though differences are modest compared to overall variability. |
| Age | Brain mass peaks during early adulthood and gradually declines after middle‑age due to neuronal loss and atrophy. |
| Body size | Larger individuals often have larger brains, but scaling isn’t perfectly linear—brain volume correlates more strongly with body length/height than total body weight. |

These figures come from postmortem studies and imaging research using MRI volumetry calibrated against known densities. Variability can span ±10% depending on individual health, genetics, and measurement method.
